edges.effect_quant: A 2022 meta-analysis of 10 randomized trials and 1,030 patients found peppermint oil improved global IBS symptoms versus placebo with a relative risk of not improving of 0.65. The earlier 2014 meta-analysis of 726 patients found a global-symptom improvement relative risk of 2.23.
edges.population: adults with irritable bowel syndrome taking enteric-coated peppermint oil capsules
edges.mechanism: Enteric-coated peppermint oil relaxes intestinal smooth muscle and can blunt spasm-driven discomfort, which is why it tends to help global IBS symptoms and abdominal pain more reliably than generic herbal mixtures.
edges.summary: This is one of the better-supported symptom-targeted GI supplements. Across multiple placebo-controlled trials, enteric-coated peppermint oil improves overall IBS symptoms often enough to be clinically useful, even though the benefit is still symptomatic rather than disease-modifying.
edges.caveats: The evidence quality is not perfect, and adverse events like heartburn are more common than with placebo. Benefits are usually short-term and do not guarantee durable control once the capsules are stopped.
